newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Common Fund to hold meeting on future role.
newsitem.headline: Common Fund to hold meeting on future role.

text.p: The Common Fund for Commodities, a U.N. affiliate, will hold a three-day meeting in the Hague from October 21 to discuss its future direction and alterative uses for its capital, the fund said on Wednesday.

The fund, established by the U.N. in 1989 and with 103 countries and the European Commission as members, will consider a study on the "Functioning and Future Role of the Common Fund," prepared by three independent experts.

To date, 42 projects covering 21 commodities have been approved, of which six have been completed and 36 are under implementation. The projects have a financial worth of $93 million, roughly half of which is provided by the fund.

"We concentrate on low cost, high impact projects, involving the private sector, which have a multiplier effect and will be sustainable beyond the Common Fund's involvement," said Rolf Boehnke, the new managing director of the fund.

Following a successful workshop on commodity development in Abidjan in July, several regional follow-up meetings were planned in Africa in 1997 and 1998. A similar workshop was planned for Latin America in June, 1997.
"This will be subject to budgetary approval," Boehnke said.
The October meeting is the last one before the eighth governing council, scheduled for December 2-3 in Morocco.
